correctness.rationale: The original 24-cell root coordinate set, dot-product adjacency and all 1493 independent simplices were reconstructed. The two-state stagewise vertex matching has 717 pairs and complete acyclic Hasse verification across 5496 incidences. The signed 34x24 integral Morse boundary has only the nine specified nonzero rows; exact elimination gives rank 3, and rows (0,3,6) by columns (0,1,9) have determinant -1. The Morse CW complex has 1 zero-cell, 34 two-cells and 24 three-cells. Since its two-skeleton is simply connected with pi2=Z^34, the integral degree matrix and three primitive cancellations prove a wedge of 31 S2 and 21 S3. A separate raw-chain implementation matches Betti ranks over GF(2), GF(3) and GF(5).

evidence: Barmak (https://arxiv.org/html/1007.0418v1) Theorem 3.4 applies when a vertex belongs to no triangle; all vertices of this 24-cell graph belong to 12 triangles. Other theorems provide tools and bounds rather than its exact integral Morse matrix.

Deshpande–Singh (https://arxiv.org/html/2001.05448v2), Section 1 theorem list and Sections 3–5, cover complete multipartite, fully whiskered, paths, cycles and perfect m-ary trees; the regular eight-valent 24-cell graph is none of these.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General constructions and special-family classification theorems do not imply this exact two-degree sphere decomposition. The existence of discrete-Morse methods does not substitute for the rank-three integral attaching-degree computation.

value.rationale: This is the exact integral homotopy type of the canonical, highly symmetric four-dimensional regular 24-cell graph independence complex. The original seven-dimensional complex reduces to a mixed two- and three-sphere bouquet. The distinct-degree sphere multiplicities and trivial integral attaching torsion are a meaningful natural invariant not supplied by the face polynomial, general graph connectivity or prior special-family theorems. No arbitrary parameter selection or speculative generalization is used.
